name: Chelbesa Washing Station
story: Smallholder cherry from the Gedeb woreda, processed at a community washing station at ~2,100 masl.

name: Hambela Estate
story: Family-run estate in the Hambela Wamena district, drying naturals on raised beds for 18–21 days.

name: Finca El Mirador
story: Third-generation 12-hectare farm near Pitalito; meticulous cherry sorting and slow parabolic drying.

name: Gatomboya Factory
story: A Karatina-area factory of the Barichu cooperative society, famous for double-fermented washed SL cultivars.

name: Finca La Bendición
story: High-mountain family farm near La Libertad; shade-grown under native inga trees at up to 1,950 masl.

name: Fazenda Boa Vista
story: Fourth-generation fazenda near Patrocínio combining mechanized harvest with careful raised-bed finishing.

name: Micro-beneficio Cumbres del Sol
story: Family micro-mill in San Marcos processing neighbors' cherry into white, red and black honey lots.

name: Finca Los Vientos
story: Small Geisha-focused farm on the eastern face of Volcán Barú, harvested in multiple selective passes.
